Title: The Default Secure Port
QuestionDetail: By default, HTTPS traffic uses which TCP port?
AnswerDetails: HTTPS defaults to port 443, while plain HTTP defaults to 80. Port 21 is FTP control and 8080 is a common alternate HTTP port for development servers.
CustomInstruction: All four are real ports you have probably seen. Pick the one a browser assumes when the URL has no port.

Title: What an A Record Returns
QuestionDetail: In DNS, an A record maps a hostname to what?
AnswerDetails: An A record returns an IPv4 address. AAAA records return IPv6 addresses, MX records point to mail servers, and CNAME records alias one hostname to another.
CustomInstruction: Each wrong option is the job of a different record type. Match the letter to the right one.

Title: Whose Fault Is It
QuestionDetail: In HTTP, which status code class indicates that the server failed to handle an otherwise valid request?
AnswerDetails: 5xx codes indicate server-side errors, such as 500 Internal Server Error and 503 Service Unavailable. 4xx codes indicate a problem with the request itself.
CustomInstruction: The distinction that matters is who is at fault - the caller or the server. Choose the class that blames the server.

Title: The I in ACID
QuestionDetail: In the ACID properties of a database transaction, what does the I stand for?
AnswerDetails: Isolation means concurrent transactions do not observe each other's intermediate state. The full set is Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation and Durability.
CustomInstruction: Say the four words in order in your head. Two of the wrong options are real database concepts that are not part of the acronym.

Title: Kibibyte, Precisely
QuestionDetail: How many bytes are in one kibibyte (KiB)?
AnswerDetails: A kibibyte is exactly 1,024 bytes. The KiB unit exists specifically to distinguish 1,024 from the decimal kilobyte of 1,000 bytes.
CustomInstruction: The unit is deliberately not the decimal one. Reach for the power of two.

Title: What an Index Costs
QuestionDetail: Adding a database index to a table primarily speeds up matching reads at the cost of what?
AnswerDetails: Every insert, update and delete must also maintain the index, and the index consumes additional storage. Indexes never change query results, only how fast they are found.
CustomInstruction: An index is a trade, not free speed. Identify what has to get slower or bigger in exchange.

Title: Halving the Haystack
QuestionDetail: What is the time complexity of binary search on a sorted array?
AnswerDetails: Each comparison halves the remaining search space, giving logarithmic time. It requires the array to be sorted first.
CustomInstruction: Think about how many times you can halve a list before one element remains, and express that as a complexity class.

Title: Born at Bell Labs
QuestionDetail: Which language was created by Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs in the early 1970s?
AnswerDetails: Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs alongside the rewriting of Unix, which made the operating system portable across hardware.
CustomInstruction: All four are from roughly the same era. Anchor on the language that Unix was rewritten in.

Title: How Git Names a Commit
QuestionDetail: In Git, each commit is identified by what?
AnswerDetails: Git identifies each commit by a cryptographic hash of its content, metadata and parent - which is why commit identifiers change when history is rewritten.
CustomInstruction: Recall what you actually paste when you cherry-pick or revert a specific commit.

Title: Safe to Retry
QuestionDetail: An operation is described as idempotent when which of the following is true?
AnswerDetails: An idempotent operation can be applied repeatedly without changing the result beyond the first application, which is what makes automatic retries safe.
CustomInstruction: This is the property that makes a retry harmless. Choose the definition that says something about repeating the call.
OptionA: It has no side effects at all
OptionC: Repeating it has the same effect as doing it once
OptionD: It always returns the same value

Title: Three Nines
QuestionDetail: An availability target of 99.9 percent allows roughly how much total downtime per year?
AnswerDetails: 99.9 percent of a 365-day year leaves about 8.8 hours of allowed downtime - a little over one working day, spread across the whole year.
CustomInstruction: Take 0.1 percent of the hours in a year and round. Do the arithmetic rather than recalling the marketing phrase.

Title: When the Network Splits
QuestionDetail: Under the CAP theorem, a distributed system experiencing a network partition must choose between which two properties?
AnswerDetails: Partition tolerance is not optional in a real network, so the live trade-off during a partition is between consistency and availability.
CustomInstruction: One of the three CAP properties is forced on you by physics. The answer is the pair you actually get to choose between.
